hendrick-theyanoguin.s: Hendrick Theyanoguin was a Mohawk leader and one of the most influential Haudenosaunee spokesmen of his time, a close ally of the British and of William Johnson. He spoke forcefully at the Albany Congress of 1754 about British neglect of the alliance.

hendrik-van-rheede.s: Hendrik van Rheede tot Drakenstein was a Dutch East India Company official and naturalist who served as commander of Malabar from 1670 to 1677. He sponsored and directed the Hortus Malabaricus, a twelve-volume study of the plants of the Malabar coast published in Amsterdam…

henny-eman.s: Henny Eman is an Aruban politician of the Aruban People's Party who became the first Prime Minister of Aruba after it gained separate status within the Kingdom of the Netherlands in 1986. He served from 1986 to 1989 and again from 1994 to 2001.

henriette-of-montbeliard.s: Henriette of Montbéliard was the heiress of the County of Montbéliard, betrothed in 1397 to Eberhard IV of Württemberg, whom she married in 1407. Through her the county passed to the house of Württemberg, which held it until the French Revolution.

henrique-paiva-couceiro.s: Henrique Paiva Couceiro was a Portuguese army officer and colonial administrator, governor-general of Angola from 1907 to 1909, and the leading royalist opponent of the First Portuguese Republic. He led royalist incursions from Spain in 1911 and 1912, and on 19 January 1919…

henry-borwin-iii-lord-of-rostock.n: Henry Borwin III, Lord of Rostock
henry-borwin-iii-lord-of-rostock.s: Henry Borwin III was a member of the Mecklenburg dynasty who received the lands around Rostock when his family's territory was divided in 1229. As the first Lord of Rostock he ruled during the rapid growth of the Hanseatic town, which had received Lübeck law in 1218.

henry-chee-dodge.s: Henry Chee Dodge was a Navajo interpreter, rancher and political leader. He served as head chief of the Navajo from 1884 and became the first chairman of the Navajo Tribal Council when it was created in 1923, chiefly to approve oil leases.

heidelberg-catechism.s: The Heidelberg Catechism is a Reformed Protestant statement of faith in question-and-answer form, published in 1563 at the order of Elector Frederick III of the Palatinate. Written chiefly by Zacharias Ursinus with Caspar Olevian, it made the Palatinate the leading Calvinist…

henry-i-duke-of-brabant.s: Henry I, Duke of Brabant, was the first ruler of the Louvain dynasty to use the title Duke of Brabant, reigning from 1183 to 1235. He founded towns, granted charters and expanded his lands between the Meuse and the Scheldt, though he was defeated by the Prince-Bishop of Liège…

henry-iii-the-white.s: Henry III the White was a Silesian Piast duke, son of Henry II the Pious, who received Wrocław when his father's duchy was divided in 1248. He ruled Wrocław from 1248 to 1266, at first jointly with his brother Władysław, and encouraged German settlement and the town's recovery…

henry-iv-of-plauen.s: Henry IV of Plauen was a member of the Reuss family of Vogtland lords who became Burgrave of Meissen and chancellor of the Kingdom of Bohemia under Ferdinand I. As a reward for his loyalty in the Schmalkaldic War he recovered Plauen and other Vogtland lands in 1547, briefly…

henry-iv-probus.s: Henry IV Probus was Duke of Wrocław from 1270 and High Duke of Poland at Kraków from 1288 to 1290. Raised at the Bohemian court, he was a patron of German poetry and wrote verse in Middle High German himself.

henry-jennings.s: Henry Jennings was an English privateer and pirate based in Jamaica and the Bahamas. In 1716 he raided the Spanish salvage camps of the wrecked 1715 treasure fleet off Florida, and he became one of the leading captains of the pirate community at Nassau.

henry-julius-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg.s: Henry Julius, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, ruled the Principality of Wolfenbüttel from 1589 and was administrator of the Prince-Bishopric of Halberstadt from 1566. A learned prince, he wrote plays, founded a court theatre and served as an adviser to Emperor Rudolf II in Prague.

henry-count-of-portugal.s: Henry, Count of Portugal, was a Burgundian noble who fought for Alfonso VI of León against the Almoravids. Around 1096 he married Alfonso's daughter Teresa and received the County of Portugal, including Coimbra.

henry-parkes.s: Henry Parkes was an English-born journalist and politician who served five times as premier of New South Wales between 1872 and 1891. He promoted free public education and free trade.

henry-raspe.s: Henry Raspe was Landgrave of Thuringia from 1227 to 1247, the last of the Ludowingian dynasty. He first acted as regent for his nephew after the death of his brother Louis IV, husband of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary.

henry-i-duke-of-munsterberg.s: Henry I, Duke of Münsterberg, known as the Elder, was a son of the Bohemian king George of Poděbrady. He held the Silesian Duchy of Münsterberg and the County of Kladsko (Glatz), which he received in 1472, and founded the Poděbrady line of Silesian dukes.

henry-iii-margrave-of-meissen.s: Henry III, Margrave of Meissen, called the Illustrious, was a Wettin prince who ruled Meissen from 1221. Through his mother, a Ludowingian, he claimed Thuringia after the death of Henry Raspe and won it in the War of the Thuringian Succession by 1264.

henry-xiii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Henry XIII, Duke of Bavaria, was a Wittelsbach prince who received Lower Bavaria, with Landshut as his seat, when he and his brother Louis II the Strict divided the duchy in 1255. The partition began the long series of Wittelsbach divisions of Bavaria.

henry-xvi-duke-of-bavaria.s: Henry XVI, Duke of Bavaria, known as the Rich, ruled Bavaria-Landshut from 1393 to 1450. A careful administrator, he built up a great treasure from silver, salt tolls and taxes.

heraclius-the-elder.s: Heraclius the Elder was a Byzantine general of Armenian origin who served against the Persians and became Exarch of Africa at Carthage. In 608 he rebelled against the emperor Phocas, sending his son Heraclius by sea and his nephew Nicetas overland to Egypt.

herbert-ii-count-of-vermandois.s: Herbert II, Count of Vermandois, was a Carolingian descendant and the most powerful magnate of northern France in the 920s. He held King Charles the Simple prisoner at Péronne from 923 until the king's death in 929 and secured the archbishopric of Reims for his young son.

herbert-kitchener.s: Herbert Kitchener was a British army officer who, as Sirdar of the Egyptian army, led the reconquest of Sudan and destroyed the Mahdist army at Omdurman in 1898. He became the first governor-general of Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, later commanded in the Second Boer War and in India,…

herceg-novi.s: Herceg Novi is a fortified port at the entrance to the Bay of Kotor in present-day Montenegro. Founded as Novi in 1382 by Tvrtko I of Bosnia, it was developed by Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, Herceg of Saint Sava, whose title gave the town its name.

herius-asinius.s: Herius Asinius was a commander of the Marrucini, an Italic people of the Adriatic coast, during the Social War against Rome. He led his people's forces on the side of the Italian allies and was killed in battle in 90 BCE.

hermann-balk.s: Hermann Balk was a knight of the Teutonic Order who led its first campaigns in Prussia from 1230, founding Thorn, Kulm and Elbing. After the Livonian Brothers of the Sword were crushed at Saule in 1236, he became the first master of the Order in Livonia in 1237, absorbing the…

hermann-goring.s: Hermann Göring was a leading Nazi, a First World War fighter pilot who became commander of the Luftwaffe and Hitler's designated successor. As minister-president of Prussia from 1933 he founded the Gestapo and used the Prussian police against the regime's opponents.

hermann-of-buxhoeveden.s: Hermann of Buxhoeveden was a German churchman, brother of Bishop Albert of Riga, who was made bishop of the Estonians in 1220. After the capture of Tartu in 1224 he moved his see there, founding the Bishopric of Dorpat, which he ruled until his death.

hermann-von-wissmann.s: Hermann von Wissmann was a German explorer and colonial officer who crossed Central Africa twice in the 1880s. In 1889 he was appointed imperial commissioner to suppress the Abushiri revolt on the East African coast, which he did with a force of African mercenaries.

hermann-wesel.s: Hermann Wesel was the last Bishop of Dorpat, elected in 1554. When the armies of Ivan IV took Dorpat in 1558 at the start of the Livonian War, he surrendered the city and was carried off to Russia, where he died in captivity.

hermanus-steyn.s: Hermanus Steyn was a burgher of the Swellendam district of the Dutch Cape Colony. In June 1795, after the settlers expelled the Dutch East India Company's landdrost, he was chosen president of their assembly of national representatives in the short-lived Swellendam Republic.

hermenegildo-gutierrez.s: Hermenegildo Gutiérrez was a Galician noble in the service of Alfonso III of Asturias. In 878 he captured Coimbra on the Mondego from the Emirate of Córdoba and became the first count of the frontier County of Coimbra.

hernandarias.s: Hernandarias, Hernando Arias de Saavedra, was born in Asunción and was the first American-born governor of the Río de la Plata, holding office several times between 1592 and 1618. He explored the interior, promoted cattle ranching and invited the Jesuits to found missions…

herod-agrippa-i.s: Herod Agrippa I was a grandson of Herod the Great, raised in Rome and a friend of the emperors Caligula and Claudius. Caligula gave him the former Tetrarchy of Philip with the title of king in 37, and by 41 Claudius had added Judaea and Samaria, reuniting his grandfather's realm.

hibatullah-akhundzada.s: Hibatullah Akhundzada is an Afghan cleric and Islamic jurist who became leader of the Taliban in 2016. After the Taliban took Kabul in August 2021 and restored the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, he became its supreme leader.

hiero-ii-of-syracuse.s: Hiero II of Syracuse was a general who seized power in Syracuse and took the title of king after defeating the Mamertines at the Longanus river around 265 BCE. Early in the First Punic War he allied with Rome in 263 BCE and remained a loyal ally until his death.

high-king-of-ireland.s: The High King of Ireland, Ard Rí in Irish, was the title claimed by kings who asserted supremacy over the island's many kingdoms. Long associated with Tara and the Uí Néill, it became a real prize from the late 10th century, when Brian Bóruma of Munster took it in 1002.

hikayat-merong-mahawangsa.s: The Hikayat Merong Mahawangsa, also called the Kedah Annals, is a Malay chronicle of the kingdom of Kedah. It traces the royal line to Merong Mahawangsa, a legendary founder, and describes the ruler's conversion to Islam.

hikayat-tanah-hitu.s: The Hikayat Tanah Hitu is a Malay chronicle of Hitu on Ambon Island, written in the mid-17th century by Imam Rijali, a Hitu leader who fled the Dutch. It recounts the origins of Hitu's rulers, the coming of Islam and the wars against the Portuguese and the Dutch East India…

hill-complex-great-zimbabwe.s: The Hill Complex is the oldest part of Great Zimbabwe, a group of stone enclosures built among the granite boulders of a steep hill overlooking the valley. Construction began in the 11th or 12th century, and the complex is thought to have been the residence of the kings and a…

himmat-singh-of-idar.s: Himmat Singh was the last Maharaja of Idar, a Rajput princely state in northern Gujarat, ruling from 1931 to 1949. The capital Ahmednagar was renamed Himmatnagar after him.

hinrich-lohse.s: Hinrich Lohse was a Nazi politician, Gauleiter of Schleswig-Holstein from 1925. From 1941 to 1944 he was Reich Commissioner of Reichskommissariat Ostland, governing the occupied Baltic states and western Belarus from Riga, where his administration took part in the persecution…

hiralal-shastri.s: Hiralal Shastri was an Indian independence activist and social reformer from Jaipur, founder of the Vanasthali Vidyapith women's college. In 1949 he became the first chief minister of the United State of Rajasthan, leading the elected ministry that governed the union of former…

hisham-ii.s: Hisham II was the third Umayyad Caliph of Córdoba, succeeding as a child in 976. Real power lay with the hajib Almanzor and his sons, while Hisham was kept secluded.

hasankeyf.s: Hasankeyf, medieval Hisn Kayfa, is an ancient town on the Tigris in south-eastern Turkey. It was the seat of the Artuqids from 1102 and of a branch of the Ayyubids from 1232 into the 15th century, who built its great bridge, mosques and palaces.

hjalmar-mae.s: Hjalmar Mäe was an Estonian politician of the far-right Vaps movement who headed the Estonian Self-Administration set up by the German occupiers from 1941 to 1944. His administration operated under the Generalkommissariat Estland within Reichskommissariat Ostland.

ho-chi-minh-trail.s: The Ho Chi Minh Trail was a network of roads, tracks and river routes running from North Vietnam through Laos and Cambodia to South Vietnam. North Vietnam used it from 1959 to send troops and supplies to the southern insurgency.

ho-han-thuong.s: Hồ Hán Thương was the second and last emperor of the Hồ dynasty of Vietnam, reigning from 1401 to 1407, while his father Hồ Quý Ly kept real power. Their state of Đại Ngu fell to the invading Ming army in 1407, and father and son were captured and taken to China, beginning two…

hoa-hao.s: Hòa Hảo is a Vietnamese Buddhist reform movement founded in 1939 by Huỳnh Phú Sổ in the Mekong Delta village of Hòa Hảo. It stresses simple lay devotion over temples and clergy and quickly won a mass peasant following.

hojo-ujimasa.s: Hōjō Ujimasa was the fourth head of the Later Hōjō clan, ruling much of the Kantō from Odawara. He continued his father Ujiyasu's wars against the Takeda and Uesugi.

hojo-ujiyasu.s: Hōjō Ujiyasu was the third head of the Later Hōjō clan and one of the leading Sengoku warlords. His night attack at Kawagoe in 1546 broke a coalition of the Uesugi and made the Hōjō masters of the Kantō.

holy-cross-minster.s: The Holy Cross Minster is the main church of Schwäbisch Gmünd in southern Germany. Its choir, begun in 1351 by Heinrich Parler, is an early and influential example of the late Gothic hall church in Germany.

holy-land.s: The Holy Land is the region between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean, roughly ancient Israel and Palestine, held sacred by Jews, Christians and Muslims. Medieval Europeans used the term for the places of Christ's life, the goal of pilgrimage and of the Crusades.

honda-tadakatsu.s: Honda Tadakatsu was one of the four great generals of Tokugawa Ieyasu, famed for fighting in dozens of battles without being seriously wounded. After the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 he received the Kuwana domain with 100,000 koku, where he rebuilt the castle and laid out the…

honda-tadamasa.s: Honda Tadamasa was a daimyo, eldest son of Honda Tadakatsu, who succeeded to Kuwana and in 1617 was moved to the Himeji domain. His son married Senhime, granddaughter of Tokugawa Ieyasu, tying the family closely to the shogunate.

hong-rengan.s: Hong Rengan was a cousin of Hong Xiuquan who learned of Western ways from missionaries in Hong Kong. Arriving at Nanjing in 1859, he became prime minister of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom with the title Shield King and proposed railways, banks, a postal service and newspapers…

horio-yoshiharu.s: Horio Yoshiharu was a daimyo who served Toyotomi Hideyoshi and then sided with Tokugawa Ieyasu. After Sekigahara his family received Izumo and Oki, and he directed the building of Matsue castle on Lake Shinji, completed in 1611, the year he died.

hosein-qoli-khan-qajar.s: Hosein Qoli Khan Qajar was the last governor, or sardar, of the Erivan Khanate for Qajar Iran, appointed in 1807. He defended Erivan against Russian attacks and built the Sardar's Palace in its fortress.

hosseinqoli-khan-bakhtiari.s: Hosseinqoli Khan Bakhtiari was a chief of the Haft Lang Bakhtiari who united the confederation of the Zagros under his leadership. In 1867 the Qajar government recognised him as ilkhan, paramount chief, of all the Bakhtiari.

hoshang-shah.s: Hoshang Shah was the second Sultan of Malwa, reigning from 1406 to 1435, son of the dynasty's founder Dilawar Khan Ghuri. He moved the capital from Dhar to the hill fortress of Mandu, which he fortified, and fought Gujarat and neighbouring Rajput states.

hoshina-masayuki.s: Hoshina Masayuki was a son of the shogun Tokugawa Hidetada and half-brother of Iemitsu, raised in the Hoshina family. Given Aizu in 1643, he founded the line that held it until 1868, and he served as guardian of the young shogun Ietsuna.

hosni-mubarak.s: Hosni Mubarak was an Egyptian air force commander who became vice-president and, after Anwar Sadat's assassination in 1981, president of Egypt. He kept the peace with Israel, relied on emergency laws and close ties with the United States, and ruled for almost thirty years.

hosokawa-shigekata.s: Hosokawa Shigekata was daimyo of Kumamoto from 1747 and one of the noted domain reformers of the Edo period. He restored the domain's finances, reorganised its administration and criminal law, and promoted local products.

hosokawa-tadaoki.s: Hosokawa Tadaoki was a samurai and tea master who fought for Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara in 1600. His wife, the Christian Hosokawa Gracia, died rather than be taken hostage by Ieyasu's enemies.

hosokawa-tadatoshi.s: Hosokawa Tadatoshi was the son of Hosokawa Tadaoki and daimyo of Kokura, transferred in 1632 to Kumamoto in Higo with 540,000 koku after the shogunate removed the Katō family. His family held Kumamoto until 1871.

hotu-matua.s: Hotu Matuʻa is the legendary founding chief of Rapa Nui (Easter Island). Island tradition says he sailed from a homeland called Hiva, landed at Anakena Bay and divided the island among his sons, ancestors of its clans.

hotula-khan.s: Hotula Khan was a khan of the Khamag Mongol confederation in the mid-12th century, son of Khabul Khan and uncle of Yesügei. Elected after the Tatars handed Ambaghai Khan to the Jin, he waged wars of revenge against the Tatars.

hovhannes-kajaznuni.s: Hovhannes Kajaznuni was an Armenian architect and leader of the Armenian Revolutionary Federation who served as the first prime minister of the First Republic of Armenia from 1918 to 1919. In 1923 he published a critical report on his party's record.

hubert-lyautey.s: Hubert Lyautey was a French general and the first resident-general of the French protectorate in Morocco, from 1912 to 1925. He ruled through the sultan and the makhzen, made Rabat the capital, built new European towns beside the old medinas and conducted long campaigns in the…

hubert-maga.s: Hubert Maga was a schoolteacher from northern Dahomey who became one of the colony's three leading politicians. He was the first president of independent Dahomey from 1960 until a coup in 1963, and returned as head of a rotating presidential council in 1970, before Mathieu…

hubert-murray.s: Hubert Murray was an Australian lawyer who governed Papua as lieutenant-governor from 1908 until his death in 1940. His long administration was paternalistic, restricting land alienation and forced labour while limiting economic development.

hudhayl-ibn-khalaf-ibn-razin.s: Hudhayl ibn Khalaf ibn Razin was a Berber chief of the Banu Razin who made Albarracín independent around 1012, as the Caliphate of Córdoba broke apart. He ruled the mountainous Taifa of Albarracín until 1045, keeping it independent between the larger taifas of Toledo, Zaragoza…

hudson-valley.s: The Hudson Valley is the valley of the Hudson River in New York, running north from New York City towards Albany. The Dutch settled it as the core of New Netherland, granting large patroonships such as Rensselaerswyck.

hugh-low.s: Hugh Low was a British colonial administrator and naturalist. He served in Labuan from 1848, first as colonial secretary, and in 1851 made the first recorded ascent of Mount Kinabalu's summit plateau.

hugh-maguire-lord-of-fermanagh.s: Hugh Maguire was Lord of Fermanagh from 1589 and one of the Irish leaders of the Nine Years' War against English rule. His resistance to an English sheriff began the conflict in 1593, and he won a victory at the Ford of the Biscuits in 1594.

hugh-of-bruyeres.s: Hugh of Bruyeres was a crusader knight from Champagne who received the Barony of Karytaina, one of the largest fiefs of the Principality of Achaea, around 1209. He held the Skorta highlands of the upper Alpheios valley.

hugh-of-ibelin.s: Hugh of Ibelin was the eldest son of Barisan of Ibelin and lord of Ibelin and Ramla in the Kingdom of Jerusalem. He was captured by Nur ad-Din's forces in 1157 and ransomed, and he married Agnes of Courtenay, former wife of King Amalric.

hugh-of-vermandois.s: Hugh of Vermandois was a younger son of King Henry I of France who became Count of Vermandois by marriage to its heiress Adelaide. He was among the leaders of the First Crusade, but returned to France after the capture of Antioch in 1098.

hugh-roe-macmahon.s: Hugh Roe MacMahon was lord of Monaghan, the MacMahon lordship of Oriel in Ulster. After he was recognised by the English administration, the Lord Deputy William Fitzwilliam had him arrested, tried and hanged in 1590.

hugo-chavez.s: Hugo Chávez was a Venezuelan army officer who led a failed coup in 1992 and was elected president in 1998. A new constitution in 1999 renamed the country the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

hugo-von-montfort.s: Hugo von Montfort was a count of the Bregenz line of the Montfort family and a Habsburg official who served as governor of Styria. He is best known as a poet: his German songs, letters and speeches, many with melodies, survive in a manuscript at Heidelberg and make him one of…

hujr-akil-al-murar.s: Hujr Akil al-Murar was a chief of the Kinda tribe and the founder of the Kingdom of Kinda in central Arabia. In the 5th century the Himyarite kings installed him as king over the Ma'add tribes of Najd.

huldrych-zwingli.s: Huldrych Zwingli was a Swiss priest and leader of the Reformation in Zürich. After serving as parish priest at Glarus, he moved to Zürich in 1519, where his preaching led the city to abolish the Mass in 1525.

humbert-ii-of-viennois.s: Humbert II of Viennois was the last independent Dauphin of the Viennois, ruling from 1333. He founded a university at Grenoble in 1339 and led a papal crusade to Smyrna in 1345 to 1347.

humbert-i-count-of-savoy.s: Humbert I, known as White-Hands, was a noble of the Kingdom of Arles who held lands around Maurienne and Savoy from about 1003. He gained control of Alpine passes and was rewarded by Emperor Conrad II for his support.

humphrey-ii-of-toron.s: Humphrey II of Toron was lord of Toron and constable of the Kingdom of Jerusalem from 1152. He was trusted as a negotiator by Muslim rulers, including Saladin, and fought in many campaigns.

hundred-years-war.s: The Hundred Years' War was a series of conflicts between the kings of England and France from 1337 to 1453, caused by disputes over Gascony and English claims to the French crown. English victories at Crécy, Poitiers and Agincourt were reversed after Joan of Arc's intervention…

hurricane-irma.s: Hurricane Irma was a Category 5 Atlantic hurricane that struck the northern Caribbean in September 2017, one of the strongest recorded in the open Atlantic. It destroyed most buildings on Barbuda, forcing the evacuation of the whole island, and devastated Sint Maarten and…

hurricane-maria.s: Hurricane Maria was a Category 5 hurricane that struck the eastern Caribbean in September 2017, two weeks after Hurricane Irma. It caused catastrophic damage on Dominica and then crossed Puerto Rico, destroying its power grid; studies estimated around 3,000 deaths there in the…

husain-shah-langah.s: Husain Shah Langah was the most important ruler of the Langah Sultanate of Multan in the second half of the 15th century. During a reign of about three decades he repelled attacks by Bahlul Lodi of Delhi and extended his rule along the Indus towards Sindh, while Multan…

husam-al-din-choban.s: Husam al-Din Choban was a commander of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum who received the frontier district of Kastamonu in the early 13th century. Around 1220 he led the Seljuk naval expedition across the Black Sea against Sudak in the Crimea.

husayn-ali-khan-of-quba.s: Husayn Ali Khan was khan of Quba in the north-eastern Caucasus. After the death of Nader Shah in 1747 he ruled as an effectively independent khan and moved his seat to the new town of Quba.

husayn-ibn-ahmad-al-habili.s: Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Habili was the sharif of Beihan, a small emirate on the frontier between the Aden Protectorate and Yemen. One of Britain's firmest allies in southern Arabia, he resisted Yemeni claims to the border in the 1950s and was a founding figure of the Federation of…

husayn-ibn-salamah.s: Husayn ibn Salamah was a Nubian freedman who served as regent and chief minister of the Ziyadid dynasty of Zabid in Yemen in the late 10th century. He held the real power in the state, built mosques and fortified towns, and constructed roads and wells linking Zabid with Mecca…

husayn-sufi.s: Husayn Sufi was a leader of the Qungrat tribe who made himself independent ruler of Khwarazm around 1361, as the Golden Horde fell into civil war. Ruling from Urgench, he founded the Sufi dynasty and seized southern Khwarazm, including Khiva and Kath.

huseyngulu-khan.s: Huseyngulu Khan was the last khan of Baku, ruling from 1792. In 1806 the Russian commander Pavel Tsitsianov came to accept the city's surrender and was killed at its gates by the khan's men.

huynh-tan-phat.s: Huỳnh Tấn Phát was a Vietnamese architect and communist politician who helped found the National Liberation Front. From 1969 he was chairman of the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam, the southern insurgency's government during the Paris…

house-of-la-marck.s: The House of La Marck was a noble family from the County of Mark in Westphalia, one of whose branches rose to power in the Ardennes from the 15th century. Its members gained control of the Duchy of Bouillon and the principality of Sedan, which they ruled as near-independent…

henri-de-la-tour-d-auvergne-viscount-of-.n: Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Viscount of Turenne
henri-de-la-tour-d-auvergne-viscount-of-.s: Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Viscount of Turenne, was one of the greatest French generals, born at Sedan, the son of its sovereign prince. He commanded in the Thirty Years' War, the Fronde and the Franco-Dutch War, becoming Marshal General of France.

hendrik-verwoerd.s: Hendrik Verwoerd was a South African National Party politician, minister of native affairs from 1950 and prime minister from 1958 to 1966. He was the principal architect of grand apartheid, including the Bantustan system.

hans-adam-i-prince-of-liechtenstein.s: Hans-Adam I, born Johann Adam Andreas, was prince of Liechtenstein from 1684 to 1712 and a wealthy Austrian magnate. To win his family a seat in the Imperial Diet he bought the Lordship of Schellenberg in 1699 and the County of Vaduz in 1712, which were united in 1719 as the…

hedwig-of-silesia.s: Hedwig of Silesia was a daughter of the counts of Andechs, dukes of Merania, and wife of Duke Henry I the Bearded of Silesia. With her husband she founded the Cistercian convent at Trzebnica and supported German settlement and new towns.

heidelberg-university.s: Heidelberg University was founded in 1386 by Rupert I, Elector Palatine, and is the oldest university in present-day Germany. It was a centre of humanism and, after the Electoral Palatinate became Calvinist, of Reformed theology, associated with the Heidelberg Catechism of 1563.
